name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 9, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:00 p.m., on February 9, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 04, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  Council Member Schlicht

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel and Director of Public Services (Animal Shelter);
  Threat to Public Services or Facilities Pursuant to paragraph (e) of Section 54954.5.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with four Council Members present (Council Member Schlicht was
absent.)
City Council Minutes  1  February 9, 2016
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received advice and gave direction to staff
but no reportable action occurred in Closed Session.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize the 2015 Employees of the Year

  Mayor Ury presented plaques to (1) Senior Planner, Tim Martin, City of Mission Viejo
  Employee of the Year; (2) Fire Captain/Paramedic Eric Leverenz, Orange County Fire
  Authority Employee of the Year; and (3) Deputy Jeff Flaming, Orange County Sheriff's
  Department Employee of the Year.

P2.  Presentation by Orange County Fire Authority Division Chief John Abel

  Chief Abel presented information on Emergency Service Delivery Enhancement in
  Mission Viejo.
P3.
  Presentation by OCSD Lieutenant Brad NewMyer on "Safety and Situational
  Awareness"

  Lieutenant NewMyer made a presentation on safety and situational awareness.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Dave Leckness, Orange County Mosquito and Vector Control District Board Member, M.V.:
provided information on activity at the Vector Control District, including background on deaths in
Orange County from West Nile Virus last year.

Lisa Willard, Coto de Caza: discussed programs and services that Alzheimer's Orange County
provides for families dealing with Alzheimer's and other related dementia.

Tonya Brown, Dana Point: announced that she is reaching out to local cities to invite residents to
her program on mental wellness and overcoming adversities in life. The program will be held the
1st Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. at the Murray Center in Mission Viejo.

Casey Cooper, Ph.D. M.V.: expressed concern about a situation in her neighborhood and stated
that the City's Code Enforcement department needs more resources in order to respond to the
community's needs.

City Council Minutes  2  February 9, 2016
 Rhonda Reardon, M.V.: speaking on behalf of Senator Patricia Bates, she extended an invitation
to the Council Members and residents to attend South Orange County Senior Day on March 11,
2016, from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center.

Hannah Hess and Donovan Higbee, M.V.: introduced themselves as staff members for
Congresswoman Mimi Walters and stated that they are available to assist wherever they can.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 6 and 7 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Schlicht

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been ready by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 26, 2016, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register Dated January 15, 2016 in the Amount of $640,820.02

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated January 22, 2016 in the Amount of $949,270.65

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Water Efficient Landscape Ordinance

City Council Minutes  3  February 9, 2016
   Adopted Ordinance 16-312 Amending Chapter 8.12 of the Mission Viejo Municipal code
  entitled "Water Efficient Landscape Regulations."

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

6.  Ferrocarril Slope Repair

  City Engineer Rich Schlesinger presented the staff report.

  Liliana Hernandez, M.V.: discussed the damage to her property after the Ferrocarril
  landslide which affected her family's sense of security and peace of mind. She stated that
  she is grateful for the City's help but the repair work that was done did not entirely fix the
  problem and there are still safety factors.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Ury, to (1) direct the City
  Manager to cease further efforts to form an Assessment District to finance the Ferrocarril
  slope repair; and (2) direct the City Manager to send a letter to Cal OES requesting the de-
  obligation of the $850,000.00 grant for the Ferrocarril slope repair.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Schlicht

7.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape and Facility Maintenance - Contract Area 1

  Council Member Sachs expressed concern with the idea of awarding the agreement to
  someone who underbid the contract.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to reject all bids and
  continue existing contract with Merchants Landscape Services, Inc. for Landscape and
  Facility Maintenance - Contract Area 1 - and direct staff to provide a detailed quarterly
  report on the contractor's performance.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Schlicht

City Council Minutes  4  February 9, 2016
 OLD BUSINESS

8.  Implied Subsidy as a Component of the Retiree Healthcare Plan June 30, 2015,
  Actuarial Valuation

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Ury, to direct staff to pay
  $347,000 out of the $500,000 (unfunded liability reserve) to get the City 100% funded on
  the RIP plan and to not fund the Implied Subsidy.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Schlicht

NEW BUSINESS

9.  Project Management Contract for the Marguerite Aquatics Complex Rehabilitation

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report
  and answered the City Council Members questions.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Ury, to award a contract
  for the Project Management Services to Griffin Structures (A16-01) in an amount not to
  exceed $75,175 and issue a purchase order.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Schlicht

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

10.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

City Council Minutes  5  February 9, 2016
 11.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

12.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

13.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

14.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths informed residents of the Driving Miz Daisy vintage flea market on the
2nd Sunday of every month at Saddleback College from 8 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. He also announced
that he is a member of the Mission Viejo Rotary Club and he has been asked to head up the Rotary’s
annual fundraiser which is a Texas Hold ‘Em tournament. It will be held on June 11, 2016, at the
Murray Center and the buy-in is $60.00, with $50.00 going to the charity of the player’s choice.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs thanked the City Manager for having Santa Margarita Water District
(SMWD) contact him about the condition of the streets in the development where he lives. He
received a visit from some representatives of the District who explained that they have only
accomplished the first part of the project. Council Member Sachs said that he has learned that he
needs to fully understand a problem before he complains about it in the future and he reiterated his
thanks to the SMWD representatives for taking their time to explain the process to him.

City Council Minutes  6  February 9, 2016
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht was absent.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum outlined her attendance at the Relay for Life kick-off event and she
encouraged residents to get involved in the Relay which will be held the first weekend in June. She
also discussed her attendance at the Jenny Finch Softball Camp and she noted that softball and
baseball opening days are coming up at the end of the month. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum discussed
the South Orange County Economic Coalition’s “Economic Report” event which has held at
Saddleback College. She thanked the Economic Coalition for partnering with the College and the
City and she said it was a great presentation. She also noted that the City has excellent partnerships
with the all of the school districts in town. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum announced that unity is the
Community of Character word of the month. She put unity into the context of the Neighborhood
Watch program that was mentioned earlier and stated that if people work together they can make
a difference. Residents should watch out for their neighbors and if they see something, say
something. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum encouraged senior residents and their families to attend the
South Orange County Senior Day on Friday, March 11, 2016, at the Norman P. Murray
Community Center. She thanked Senator Pat Bates for hosting the program and for her continued
support of the senior community. She also thanked Rhonda Reardon for congratulating her on the
award she received and she too congratulated Kevin Frabotta, General Manager of Lake Mission
Viejo Association who won an award for innovative management for a new water purification
system. In closing, she invited residents to join her for her monthly “Walk with Wendy” on
Saturday, February 13 beginning at 8:00 a.m. at the back door of the Murray Center.

Mayor Ury

15.  Purchase of Smart Technology Controllers for City of Mission Viejo City Facilities
  and Sports Parks

  Mayor Ury presented his report.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to (1) appropriate
  $238,376 for the purchase and installation of the Smart Technology Controllers for the
  larger 22 City Facilities and Sports Parks from the General Fund. The purchase to be funded
  by using rebate funds (Estimated to be $99,605) obtained from the Metropolitan Water
  District, and $138,771 from the General Fund to complete the purchase; and (2) authorize
  City Staff to process a contract and issue a purchase order to Signature Control Systems in
  an amount not to exceed $238,376.00.

City Council Minutes  7  February 9, 2016
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Schlicht

Mayor Ury discussed his attendance at the Jenny Finch Softball Camp. He noted that Ms. Finch
is six feet two inches tall, the nicest person and the best softball player ever. He commented on
the South Orange County Economic Coalition meeting and he encouraged his colleagues to get a
copy of the Economic Report presentation. Mayor Ury stated that as much as everyone wants to
have economic development in South Orange County, there is not a single square foot of industrial
or commercial space available south of Irvine. He noted that many employees living in South
County are forced to go distances for work and he hopes that there will be progress made in that
area. Mayor Ury also discussed the aging population in South County and highlighted that we are
losing people between the ages of 23 and 35. He stated that the Economic Report is an extremely
valuable presentation and he again encouraged his colleagues to take a look at it.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:09 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, February 23, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 23, 2016

City Council Minutes  8  February 9, 2016
